newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat to visit Egypt again on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to visit Egypt again on Saturday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Egypt on Saturday for the second time in four days for more talks on Egypt's quest for a breakthrough between Israel and the Palestinians, official sources said on Friday.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is at the centre of efforts to bridge the differences between the two sides, which mainly centre on Israeli settlement activities in Arab East Jerusalem.

Diplomatic sources said Egypt and the Palestinians were working on a five-point plan which includes a freeze on any change in the status of Jerusalem and a ban on Jewish settlement of the West Bank for "a sufficient period".
In return the Palestinians would give a firm commitment to address Israel's security demands, they added.
But the sources said the gap between the two sides remained very wide, especially on the question of Jewish settlements.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to rescind a decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on an East Jerusalem site known to Israelis as Har Homa and to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Thursday,"It's far too early to be talking about openings especially after the statements made by Israel, and these are statements that are very damaging to any initiative and any action that can lead to an easing (in the situation)," Moussa said.
The European Union's special envoy to the Middle East, Miguel Angel Moratinos, said on Tuesday he could see "the beginning of a solution".
Moratinos has gone to the United States, where Egyptian presidential adviser Osama el-Baz is also consulting U.S. officials on how to break the Middle East deadlock.
